      "observations": [
        "All 109 owned diff lines across three eligible paths were read. The batch getter uses an integer preference with default 500 and Math.max(..., 1). This is a lower bound, not an upper limit of 500. The getter is evaluated for each splice.",
        "Initial full fetch and both V1/V2 updates splice pending hrefs into batches and await each request/store before continuing. _multigetRequest only encodes the supplied hrefs into one REPORT and logs their count; it does not enforce a batch size itself. _fetchAndStore still distinguishes more than 25 locally added cards from per-card adds, independently of the network preference.",
        "Successful V2 completion writes the new sync token only after all batches, and each path sends its final synced notification after the loop. This does not make the whole sync atomic: earlier batches can already have stored cards when a later await rejects. Initial fetch catches per-card parse failures; _fetchAndStore does not add that catch. No mid-batch failure or atomicity test was added.",
        "The two new tasks set the preference to 1 and await the existing subtest, then clear the preference on normal completion. Their comments explicitly say the test does not prove that multiple requests occur. Full V1 subtest and every V2 difference were read: they directly check card membership, counts, names, etags, notifications and V2 token transitions. Both complete subtest bodies and test files match the fixed accepted blobs. They do not count REPORTs or assert per-request href lengths.",
        "Actual shared helpers verify server card count/etag/href/vCard content and accumulated notification arrays. Several inherited assertions omit messages, including helper deepEqual and server scalar comparisons; no assertions were added by this patch. The pre-existing initial full-fetch path still uses public deleteCards/modifyCard while incremental storage uses Internal methods; batching does not repair or establish read-only behavior. That broader write-contract question remains bounded.",
